title: Clarinet Quintet in A major
hook: Written for a friend’s clarinet, it lets one warm voice sing among four strings.

painting.title: Madame Vigée Le Brun and her Daughter, Julie
painting.pairingNote: Painted in 1789, the year of the quintet, it shows a moment of calm, unforced affection, the kind of warmth Mozart wrote into music for a friend.

facts: Mozart finished the quintet in Vienna on 29 September 1789, for his friend Anton Stadler, the clarinettist for whom he later wrote the Clarinet Concerto. In a letter of April 1790 Mozart called it “Stadler’s quintet”.

It was first played on 22 December 1789 at a charity concert in Vienna for the widows and orphans of musicians, with Stadler as soloist. It was heard between the two halves of a cantata by another composer.
Mozart wrote it for the [[basset-clarinet|basset clarinet]], Stadler’s instrument with extra low notes. Today it is usually played on an ordinary clarinet in A.
This is not a concerto. The clarinet leads more often than the others, but the five players share the music, and the strings often have the tune.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a calm, singing Allegro (I), a slow song for clarinet over muted strings (II), a minuet with two contrasting trios (III), a set of variations on a cheerful tune (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro
movements.summary: The strings begin alone with a calm, hymn-like theme, and the clarinet answers with a quick, rising and falling sweep of notes. That contrast, between the strings’ smooth chords and the clarinet’s brilliant runs, carries the whole movement. It is in [[sonata-form|sonata form]].

mainIdeas.name: The strings’ theme
mainIdeas.description: soft, smooth chords, moving together like a hymn.

mainIdeas.name: The clarinet’s answer
mainIdeas.description: a fast [[arpeggio|arpeggio]] that climbs up and falls back.

mainIdeas.name: The second theme
mainIdeas.description: a gentle, slightly wistful tune, first in the violin over a plucked cello, then in the clarinet.

stops.hear: The four strings alone, soft and smooth, in quiet chords
The clarinet enters with a quick run up and down
The clarinet sings a flowing line, trading phrases with the first violin
The first violin plays a gentle new tune; the cello plucks below
The clarinet takes the tune and turns it into a minor key
stops.happening: The second theme in the clarinet

stops.hear: The hymn-like opening again
The clarinet’s run leads into new keys; the instruments pass the ideas around
The clarinet sweeps up and down in long broken chords while the strings move through the harmonies
stops.happening: The clarinet’s arpeggios over changing chords

stops.hear: The strings’ calm theme in the home key, with the clarinet holding a long note above
The violin’s gentle tune over the plucked cello, now in A major

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: A quiet, unhurried close

notice: Listen for who has the tune. The strings start the movement and the first violin introduces the second theme; the clarinet often comments rather than leads.

movements.heading: Larghetto
movements.summary: A long, slow song for the clarinet over [[muted|muted]] strings, in D major. In the middle the first violin answers with rising runs, and the two seem to talk. Near the return of the song, the clarinet takes up the violin’s runs for itself.

mainIdeas.name: The song
mainIdeas.description: a slow, calm melody in the clarinet, with soft chords in the muted strings.

mainIdeas.name: The dialogue
mainIdeas.description: quick upward scales in the first violin, answered by short clarinet phrases.

stops.hear: The clarinet sings a slow, calm melody; the strings, muted, support it softly
The first violin rushes up in quick scales; the clarinet answers with short phrases
The clarinet holds long notes, falling step by step
stops.happening: A quiet passage before the return

stops.hear: Now the clarinet races up in scales of its own
The slow, calm song returns
The strings pass soft rippling figures to each other under the clarinet’s last phrases

notice: Notice the mutes on the strings. They keep the accompaniment soft and veiled, so the clarinet’s line sounds even warmer.

movements.heading: Menuetto – Trio I – Trio II
movements.key: A major – A minor – A major
movements.summary: An elegant [[minuet|minuet]] with, unusually, two [[trio|trio]]s. The first is for the strings alone, in A minor; the clarinet stays silent. The second brings the clarinet back with a rustic, country-dance tune. The minuet returns after each trio.

mainIdeas.name: The minuet
mainIdeas.description: a firm, graceful dance for all five.

mainIdeas.name: Trio I
mainIdeas.description: a shadowy tune for the strings alone, with a little grace note that gives it a sighing, catching sound.

mainIdeas.name: Trio II
mainIdeas.description: a lilting, rustic dance tune in the clarinet.

stops.hear: A firm, graceful dance, the clarinet and the strings sharing the tune
The clarinet falls silent; the strings play a quiet, shadowy tune in the minor
The graceful dance again
The clarinet leads a lilting country dance, bouncing over the strings
The dance one last time

notice: In Trio I, notice the clarinet’s silence. Mozart takes his soloist out completely, and the strings sound darker without it.

movements.heading: Allegretto con variazioni
movements.summary: A set of [[variation|variation]]s on a cheerful, march-like tune. In each variation the tune keeps its shape but changes its dress: new counter-melodies, a minor-key lament for the viola, fast runs, a slow Adagio. A short, quicker passage ends the work.

mainIdeas.name: The theme
mainIdeas.description: a bright, simple tune in the strings, in two short halves, each repeated; the clarinet joins only for a few bars.

mainIdeas.name: The variations
mainIdeas.description: each one gives a different player something new.

stops.hear: The strings play a bright, simple tune; the clarinet joins in briefly
The clarinet plays a new, decorative melody while the strings share the theme
The strings alone, then all five answering them
Darker, in the minor: the viola sings a sobbing tune
Back in the major: quick, sparkling runs in the clarinet, then the violin
The music stops on a held chord
stops.happening: A pause before the slow variation

stops.hear: Very slow and tender, like a song
Quicker again, light and cheerful

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: A brisk, happy close

notice: In Variation 3, listen for the viola. It is usually hidden in the middle of the strings; here it has the tune.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Sabine Meyer recorded the quintet in 1988 with the Wiener Streichsextett: Erich Höbarth and Peter Matzka (violins), Thomas Riebl (viola) and Rudolf Leopold (cello).

threads.title: A friend’s voice
threads.body: The quintet was written for Stadler’s playing: long, singing lines and quick runs across the whole range of his instrument.

threads.title: Five equals
threads.body: The strings often lead, and in the first trio the clarinet does not play at all.

threads.title: Smooth and brilliant
threads.body: The first movement’s contrast, smooth string chords against the clarinet’s sparkling runs, comes back in the Larghetto’s dialogue and in the finale’s variations.
